text: Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) is the major human ATP-production pathway; its deficiencies cause the largest collection of inborn errors of metabolism, yet no complete catalog of essential genes exists. Using a genome-wide CRISPR "death screen" that actively selects dying cells — exploiting the classic finding that OXPHOS-deficient cells survive in glucose but die in galactose — the authors identified 191 high-confidence hits required for OXPHOS, 72 of which underlie known OXPHOS diseases. The screen uncovered a functional module comprising NGRN, WBSCR16, RPUSD3, RPUSD4, TRUB2, and FASTKD2 that regulates mitochondrial 16S rRNA and intra-mitochondrial translation. The work yields a rich catalog of OXPHOS-essential genes and demonstrates the general power of death screening for functional genomic analysis.
